# Guarantee catalogue

**Generated** from `core_guarantees()` (`src/agent/guarantee.rs`); do not edit. Regenerate with `UPDATE_GUARANTEE_CATALOGUE=1 cargo test --lib --features compliance,a2a the_checked_in_guarantee_catalogue_is_current`. A guarantee is a claim the startup report resolves against the node as built and configured — `enforced` · `not_configured` (the setting named) · `not_in_build` (the feature named) · `not_applicable` (the role fact named) · `not_verifiable_here` (external prerequisites, never counted). The plan is `docs/plans/guarantees-and-rule-catalogue.md`; the live report is `guarantee_report()` / `GET /gateway/guarantees`.

Schema `mycelium.guarantees/1` · 38 core guarantees.

| `egress.allow_list` | 1 | egress | NodeEnforced | the substrate's own outbound calls are restricted to a hostname allow-list (MCP bridge, LLM, probes, skillrunner, the wasm host, the wiki sink, the federation client, OIDC) — the first URL and every redirect hop, with the host read the way the client reads it | `egress.allow_hosts` non-empty (empty allows all); the federation client (the node's policy applied to clients it is handed, `FederationClient::with_egress` elsewhere) and OIDC discovery + JWKS since 2026-10-03 (a denied issuer refuses `start()`). Since 2.23.0: every redirect hop re-checked (≤ 5, never https → http), none followed by a client without the policy or carrying a credential header (`mycelium::egress_client`); the host parsed with the client's own WHATWG parser; an object store gated on the endpoint it dials, not its bucket. An `HttpLibrarySource` or `OllamaProbe` built outside an agent is gated only when built `with_egress`. **Not covered:** name resolution (an allowed name resolving to a denied address), a cloud identity's credential traffic, redirects inside `object_store`'s own client | `config::EgressPolicy::permits_url` | `docs/operations/crown-jewel.md` |
| `egress.credentials` | 1 | egress | NodeEnforced | a credential binding's value is attached at the egress gate only to a request for the host it names (on its port when it names one — a binding to `localhost` or an IP literal must; under its path prefix; over https or to loopback) — refused anywhere else, dropped on a redirect that leaves it, counted per binding, and never in a log, a `Debug`, an error or the evidence journal; a caller holds only its placeholder | `[[egress_credentials]]` (or `GOSSIP_EGRESS_CREDENTIALS`), values read once at `start()`; a caller that sends through the gate — `OpenAiBackend::with_credentials`, `[[serve]]`'s `credential`, `EgressCredentials::send` / `send_once`, an `[[activation]]` command through its stem's egress proxy (`[activation.confine.egress] credentials`). **Not covered:** a secret a component or command reads from its own environment or files (an `[[activation]]` command without `[activation.confine.egress]` has no path to the gate); a proxy the gate's client is configured with (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`) sees a plaintext or loopback request's header; a placeholder in a query string or body (not resolved); `api_key` / `api_key_env`, federation, object-store and git credentials, which keep their own paths | `agent::egress_credentials::EgressCredentials::send`, `agent::egress_credentials::EgressCredentials::send_once`, `config::CredentialBinding::authorises_url` | `docs/operations/crown-jewel.md` |

| `persist.unreadable_refused` | 1 | persistence | NodeEnforced | a node does not start over persisted state it could not read — nothing is compacted over an unreadable snapshot or WAL | `[persistence]` with `on_unreadable = "refuse"` (the default) | `lifecycle (replay; `persistence::quarantine_unreadable`)`, `persistence::do_snapshot (aborts on a corrupt record)` | `docs/operations/deployment.md` |
| `at_rest.cipher` | 1 | persistence | NodeEnforced | the WAL and snapshot are encrypted at rest | `[persistence]`; `with_data_at_rest_cipher`, before `start()` | `lifecycle (cipher read once at start)` | `docs/operations/crown-jewel.md` |
| `cons.safety_profile` | 2 | consensus | NodeEnforced | an exclusive outcome — a lock, a leader, a consistent write, a commitment award, a capability-authz policy, any proposal marked safety-sensitive — is decided only by an electorate group: one pinned by member identity, decided by every member it names and frozen after, whose acceptors answer only for their own electorate | `consensus_require_electorate = true`; the electorates declared (`/gateway/govern/electorate`), one marked `exclusive_default` for the cluster-scoped verbs. Its members are fixed at genesis — changing them is a migration that terminates: declare the successor naming the group, retire the group into it (closing it), complete the carry from a majority of it, after which the predecessor is never consulted (docs/design/consensus-electorate.md §8.3); a dead member lowers the group's fault tolerance until it is migrated, a lost majority stops it and cannot migrate. The fleet's default is declared once and moves only by the holder's retirement. The effect is still the caller's to fence at the resource | `consensus::propose (the engine's door)`, `consensus::cross_propose` | `docs/design/consensus-electorate.md` |

| `fed.partner_slots` | 1 | federation | NodeEnforced | the edge carries at most a fixed number of calls from one partner at once, refusing the next rather than queuing it — per gateway, so N gateways admit N times the cap | `CallPolicy::max_in_flight_per_partner > 0` on the attached `FederationEdge` | `federation::edge::FederationEdge::admit` | `docs/operations/federation.md` |
| `fed.caller_named` | 1 | federation | NodeEnforced | a federated call made through this gateway carries the authenticated local caller's principal, never the node's and never one taken from the request | a gateway credential model (`gateway_auth_token`, or with `compliance` a token table or `[oidc]`) in front of `/gateway/federation/*`; on an open gateway every call names `anonymous` | `agent::http::federation_routes (call_as with the resolved principal)` | `docs/operations/federation.md` |

## The state matrix

A column is a configuration, a cell is the state the report would log at `start()`; what is missing or not applicable is on the report itself, not here.
